title: LOGICAL — vendor-defined storage (IBM signed-int .TRUE. = -1, others 1) — bit-test idioms break
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE FLAG_TO_INT(L, I)
C     LOGICAL's underlying integer value is implementation-defined.
C     IBM XL Fortran: .TRUE. = -1 (all bits set), .FALSE. = 0. GNU
C     Fortran: .TRUE. = 1, .FALSE. = 0. Code that converts logical
C     to integer with TRANSFER or relied on bitwise math is
C     compiler-specific. The naive Java port to (L ? 1 : 0) is
C     wrong for IBM-origin code.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      LOGICAL L
      INTEGER I
      I = TRANSFER(L, I)
      END
notes: TRANSFER(LOGICAL) gives different results across compilers. This is rare in modern code but DOES show up in legacy IBM mainframe-origin Fortran. The spec must flag the assumption and surface the platform of origin as an open question.
